title: Expose a full-rank fixed-charge counterexample with nonrare sector
statement: The explicit four-mode full-rank Gaussian product, dephased only in total number, is a mixture of five Gaussian states. Its N=2 sector has probability1/3 and state I6/12+|psi><psi|/2, psi=(|12>+|34>)/sqrt2; the Slater witness has expectation-1/12. Charge projection need not preserve convex-Gaussianity even for a commuting full-rank input.

requires: Actual Gaussian covariance or efficiently sampled component and exact charge, specified number-conserving instrument family
provides: A source-specific obstruction to reusing a positive Gaussian mixture after charge projection
assumptions: Not a counterexample to an actually qualified weak-coupling Gibbs theorem
costs: Within-component O(n^5) exact arithmetic or paid improved Pfaffian implementation, rational/precision costs
Outer rejection/second-moment/mixing costs remain unacquired; finite-bit trajectory implementation separate
contract.units: Normalized states, charge probability1/3 and dimensionless witness.
contract.obstruction: Commutation with charge and a nonrare sector do not justify a positive Gaussian transfer.

evidence.quote: ## 2. Exact full-rank counter to charge-preserving Gaussianity
evidence.range_scope: Governing producer statement; retain the complete source contract and review scope.

body: The conditional component receiver does not acquire the outer reweighted mixture p_q(a) proportional to p(a)w_q(a). Fixed-charge projection, existence of a positive mixture and an efficient acquired mixture sampler are distinct. The threshold is sector/model-specific and is not a lower bound against every classical simulation. No broad new Gibbs-sampling or hardware advantage was acquired. Read the exact supporting statement and its applicable conditions. Producer review status is preserved; no new scientific audit or producer-code execution was performed for this insertion.
